title: “IT WAS JUST FIVE LOAVES.”
paragraphs: “IT WAS JUST FIVE LOAVES.”

Not a harvest.
Not a bakery.
Just a boy’s lunch.

Five barley loaves.
Two small fish.
That’s it.

And in front of him?
A crowd that scholars estimate at 15,000–20,000 hungry people.

Men. Women. Children.
An ocean of need.
The disciples did the math first.
“Eight months’ wages wouldn’t buy enough bread for everyone to have a bite.” (John 6:7)
Translation?
Impossible.
But then Andrew noticed something.
A child.

Standing there quietly.
Holding a small meal someone had packed for him that morning.
Imagine the moment.

The boy hears grown men discussing hunger, impossibility, logistics, budgets.
And still… he steps forward.
Not with abundance.
With everything he had.

Five loaves.
Two fish.
Small hands.
Open heart.
And here’s the detail most people miss:
Jesus did not multiply the bread in the boy’s hands.
He multiplied it after it was surrendered.

Jesus took it.
He gave thanks.
Then the miracle began.

Bread breaking.
Fish dividing.
Basket after basket after basket moving through the crowd.
Until Scripture says:
“They all ate and were satisfied.” (John 6:12)
Not a taste.
Satisfied.
And when it was over?
Twelve baskets left.

The lunch that looked laughably small
became overflow in the hands of Christ.
Listen carefully.

God rarely starts with abundance.
He starts with surrender.

Moses had a staff.
David had a sling.
A widow had a jar of oil.

And one unnamed boy
had a lunch.
That’s the Gospel pattern.

You bring what feels small.
Jesus turns it into what only God can do.

Your little faith.
Your broken story.
Your imperfect offering.
Placed in the hands of Christ—
becomes more than enough.
Because the real miracle in John 6 wasn’t the bread.
It was the Bread of Life standing in front of them.
Later Jesus said:
“I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never hunger.” (John 6:35)
The crowd came for food.
But Jesus came to give eternal life.
And that life is given the same way the boy gave his lunch:

Open hands.
Full surrender.
Trust in Jesus.
So here’s the question tonight:
What are you holding that feels too small for God to use?

Your time?
Your talent?
Your faith?
Place it in the hands of Christ.
He is still multiplying surrendered lives.
And He is still feeding hungry souls.
Come to Him.

Because the Bread of Life
is more than enough.
